title: async / await
description: Async functions return Promises; await pauses until one resolves. Wrap awaits in try/catch and parallelize with Promise.all.

notes: await is only valid inside an async function (or a top-level module).
Sequential awaits run one-at-a-time — use Promise.all for independent work.
A throw inside an async function becomes a rejected Promise; catch it with try/catch around the await.

questions.q: What does an async function always return?
questions.explain: Whatever you return is wrapped in a Promise; whatever you throw becomes a rejection.

options: Only inside an async function (or top-level module)

questions.q: Two independent awaits that take the same time — fastest pattern?
questions.explain: Sequential awaits add latencies; Promise.all runs them concurrently.

questions.q: How do you catch a rejected awaited Promise?

exercises.prompt: Make the IIFE async, then await a resolved value inside it.

blanks.hint: IIFE prefix that enables await inside

exercises.prompt: Run three resolved promises in parallel and join the results.

L3.prompt: Write an async `fetchVal(x)` that returns `Promise.resolve(x * 2)`. Call it 3 times in parallel with Promise.all on inputs 1,2,3 and log the sum.
hints: Wrap everything in an immediately-invoked async function so the log fires.
Use Promise.all and destructure the result array.
